scene_script_excerpt:
SCENE 02 — A monkey rubs two sticks and starts a little flame — edit4.800s (2.333–7.133s)
Setting and framing: Keep the supplied woodland clearing, broad left tree trunk, arching leafy canopy, sage ferns, winding roots, distant blue hills and golden afternoon light. Keep the same monkey seated on the same gray stone on the left. The ground immediately in front of the monkey is clear earth with a few flat leaves; remove the old fallen log and all loose background sticks from this foreground action area. Keep the supplied locked medium-wide full-body portrait camera and subject scale. Both hands and the two touching sticks sit clearly in front of the monkey’s belly, above the quiet lowest17% reserved for captions. The crossing of the sticks must be visible in open space between the hands and the stick tips, not hidden by a fist. Keep supported feet and the single tail entirely visible.
Character: Exactly one friendly cocoa-brown storybook monkey with the same tan muzzle and belly, rounded ears, expressive dark eyes, small natural monkey mouth, ordinary compact monkey limbs and one attached long curved tail as the supplied scene. Preserve its proportions and painting. No clothes or accessories; no other characters.
First frame: The monkey looks down with quiet curiosity and holds exactly TWO SHORT WOODEN STICKS: one stick in its left hand and one in its right hand. Both are held above the ground. The left-hand stick points diagonally up-right; the right-hand stick points diagonally up-left so their exposed wood tips cross and TOUCH in front of the monkey. Both gripping hands are separated, below the crossing, leaving the wood-to-wood contact unobstructed. Include only these two plain brown sticks, each with a simple readable shaft and a few pale frayed wood fibers at the touching point. Neither stick is supported by another piece of wood. The sticks are entirely unlit: no ember, glow, smoke, sparks or flame. The monkey’s face, ears, body, feet and single curved tail match the reference. No banana, no log, no third stick, no bow/drill/fireboard apparatus, no extra hand.
Action: Begin with the two unlit sticks crossed and touching as in the first frame. During0.3–2.2s the monkey playfully rubs their upper lengths together in short back-and-forth strokes, one stick per hand, keeping both grips readable and the wood contact continuous. The sticks remain two distinct objects throughout; no separate prop enters. A faint wisp appears on the rubbed wood, then the upper ends catch little orange flames around2.4s. The monkey stops rubbing, lifts its shoulders and leans back slightly in one surprised reaction by3.2s. End with the same crossed shafts and both small flames attached to the rubbed upper ends shown in the last frame. Retain supported feet and the single tail. Continue a brief natural blink/breath and gentle wood-flame flicker through5s without freezing the whole scene. No extra hand, third stick, grip teleportation, banana, log, huge fire or body/texture ripple. This is a playful imagined cartoon accident, not an asserted historical discovery.
Last frame: Keep the exact same monkey identity, seated body, supported feet, single tail, forest, camera, clear foreground and TWO sticks from the first frame. Each hand still holds the cool lower end of its same stick, with the two shafts crossing in front of the monkey. The rubbed upper ends of BOTH sticks have now caught small orange flames: a larger tongue on the upper-right tip and a smaller tongue on the upper-left tip, attached to the wood with a little local darkening. The monkey has stopped rubbing and reacts with raised shoulders, wide eyes and a small surprised open monkey mouth. Keep the hands well below the flame and the monkey unhurt. Preserve the afternoon light and woodland geometry, adding only a faint warm reflection near the burning tips. No banana, extra stick, supporting log, floating fire or wildfire.
Narrator: “We don't know. Natural fires existed long before people.”
Speaker cue: Existing02-01-narrator, local0.800–4.596s, unchanged1x. Sol is absent.
Story scope: Playful imagined wood-rubbing vignette; no asserted identity of fire’s first discoverer. Existing dialogue unchanged.
Generation:5s, planned4.8s edit; Both exact stills approved by Elaine before animation.
Motion: Static camera. Normal-speed action on twos at final30fps: unchanged consecutive two-frame states,15 updates per second. Stable painted backdrop and texture; no interpolation, frame blending, optical flow or concealing blur. No generated speech, music, effects or text.
